CI green-ish and re-running; blocked on his > re-review and on Trang's Loom. A delegated review found a real `obsidian://` > bypass, now fixed. ## Goal / scope agreement The ticket's instruction to "reuse the geo-shape link code path" rests on a **wrong premise**: there is no app-side geo link code. The action, dialog and icon are all stock tldraw 3.14.2, gated on the duck-type `'url' in shape.props`. So the work is a storage + eligibility problem, not UI wiring. ENG-2227 reached the same conclusion on the Roam side. Agreed deviations from `Done When`, all stated in the PR body: `obsidian://` page-link support (ticket lists "a new link format" as out of scope, but its Problem statement names page links as the primary target and `T.linkUrl` cannot express one), click-gesture alignment with discourse nodes, and a pnpm patch of tldraw. **Unit tests are explicitly out at Trang's request**, which leaves the ticket's fourth `Done When` unmet. ## Approved plan ```mermaid flowchart TD A[text shape selected] --> B{patch: useHasLinkShapeSelected
'url' in props OR type === 'text'} B -->|eligible| C[stock Edit link menu item] C --> D[overrides.actions swaps onSelect only] D --> E[TextLinkDialog: text to allowlist, geo to T.linkUrl] E --> F[shape.meta.url — no schema, no migration] F --> G[TextLinkOverlay re-applies the allowlist before href] G --> H[click to sidebar · cmd to new tab · cmd+alt to split] ``` - `utils/textShapeLink.ts` — allowlist + normalisation; every protocol test derives from the parser. - `overlays/TextLinkOverlay.tsx` — the affordance, in `InFrontOfTheCanvas` beside the Relations and DragHandle overlays. - `TextLinkDialog.tsx` — the fork; reads/writes `meta` for text, `props` for everything else. - `patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch` — restores the stock menu item for meta-based links. - Deleted: the custom text shape util, `baseShapeUtils`, the migration, and the schema fallback. ship_when_verified: no ## Interventions - [2026-09-30] Trang spotted from a screenshot that the link icon sat **on top of** the text — I had verified clickability and geometry but never looked at the rendered image. - [2026-09-30] Trang had to correct me for posting four replies to Michael's threads without showing drafts first; now a standing rule in memory. - [2026-09-30] The overlay-instead-of-shape-util idea was Trang's, not mine or the reviewer's. It turned out to be the largest simplification in the change. ## Key decisions - **[2026-09-30] Store the link in `shape.meta.url`, reversing the 2026-09-14 choice of `props.url`** — *Why:* compatibility, not code volume. With `props.url` a file written by the new build and opened by an **older** build throws `Unexpected property: url` and renders a blank canvas; `meta` loads, ignores the link, and round-trips it. Canvas files are markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions. *Rejected:* `props.url`, which buys the stock props-gated menu item for free but costs the migration and the rollback hazard. *Revisit if:* cross-version file compatibility stops mattering. - **[2026-09-30] Render the icon from an overlay, not a custom `TextShapeUtil`** — *Why:* the stock text shape is never subclassed, which deletes the shape util, `baseShapeUtils` and its "two lists nothing asserts agree" hazard. *Rejected:* subclassing. *Revisit if:* rotation, frame clipping or stacking fidelity actually bites a user. - **[2026-09-30] The patch makes text shapes eligible *unconditionally*** — *Why:* geo qualifies via a `props.url` that defaults to `""`, i.e. presence is a capability claim, not state. *Rejected:* gating on `meta.url` being present — see Dead ends. *Revisit if:* a tldraw bump breaks the patch (it will, loudly); the fallback is ~40 lines of hand-built menu item. - **[2026-09-30] Did not patch `validLinkProtocols` to give geo `obsidian://` too** — *Why:* it is protocol-only, so it would admit any `obsidian:` action URI including `advanced-uri?commandid=`. Doing it safely needs the check body patched, not just the Set. *Revisit if:* Michael wants geo/text consistency. ## Dead ends - **Gating the patched predicate on `typeof meta.url === "string"`** — bootstrap deadlock: the menu item was gated on the value that only the dialog creates, and the dialog opens from the menu item. Shapes that already had a link worked perfectly, so it looked fine; a shape without one could never get its first. Types, lint, build and CI were all green. Only driving the real app caught it. - **`schemaBeforeAppMigrations`** (commits `f45e008a`, `eaaf6202`, written by a later session to patch around the required prop) — Michael flagged it as suspicious and unrelated. It became moot: moving to `meta` removes the migration entirely, so `canvasFileSync.ts` and `tldraw.ts` are now byte-identical to main. - **`pnpm patch-commit`** rewrites all of `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — requotes every key and strips every comment. Restore from `origin/main` and hand-add the one `patchedDependencies` line; the patch still applies. - **CDP harness misuse** — `evaluate()` treats any string containing `return` as a raw body (so a bare IIFE yields `undefined`), `waitFor()` only succeeds on literal `true`, and `key()` takes an options object. Getting these wrong failed all five scenarios *identically*, which reads as a product bug. ## Constraints & preferences - **No unit tests in this PR** (Trang, 2026-09-29), re-confirmed after `apps/obsidian` gained Vitest on main. Flagged once per decision; do not re-litigate. - **Never reply to a human reviewer's comments directly** — draft in chat and wait for approval. Bots are exempt. - The Loom is Trang's to record; I supply the shot list. - Teaching workspace lives in the Obsidian vault, never in a worktree. ## Gotchas / landmines - This worktree's `.env` files predate newer variables. `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` (apps/obsidian) and `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_GRAPH_URL_1` / `_EMAIL_1` / `_PASSWORD_1` (apps/roam) had to be copied from the main checkout. **One copy corrupted `apps/roam/.env`** by appending onto a line with no trailing newline, gluing a key onto `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`'s value — repaired, backup at `apps/roam/.env.bak-eng2228`. - `pnpm build` mirrors to the **slot** vault — here `testVault2`, not the `testVault` that was open. Check the `mirrored to …` line before concluding a build is stale. - `address_comments: true` on the PR monitor would auto-reply to human reviewers, which contradicts the draft-first rule. Left off deliberately; `auto_fix` also left off. - Michael's three inline threads are answered but still unresolved — only he can clear `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. ## Current state PR #1442, head `5253da0d`, 504 changed lines (over the 400 guideline; justified in the brief). Body carries a Mermaid flow, a 5-row scenario matrix with screenshots captured at the final revision, a **Not verified** section, and both unmet items stated plainly. All five CDP scenarios pass; `ci:validate` green locally and re-running on GitHub. The delegated review's confirmed findings are fixed in `5253da0d`; four lesser ones are listed in the body as raised-but-not-acted-on. ## Next step Write the Loom shot list — one shot per scenario-matrix row, in order — and hand it to Trang. Then wait for Michael's re-review. ## Open questions / blockers - **Keep the two-line tldraw patch, or drop it for ~40 lines of hand-built menu item?** Asked Michael directly in the PR comment; unanswered. It dies on the next tldraw bump either way. - Whether geo shapes should accept `obsidian://` too — needs the `linkUrl` check body patched, not just `validLinkProtocols`. Waiting on Michael. - The rollback claim is argued from file contents, not exercised against a real older build. *unchecked*

content.content:
# 2026-09-30 21:20 — ENG-2228

Reworked the implementation after Michael asked us to compare `meta.url` against the
props-schema change. Link now lives in `shape.meta.url` and the icon is drawn by a
canvas overlay, which deleted the custom text shape util, `baseShapeUtils`, the
migration and the schema fallback — so the two files he called "suspicious" are back
to identical-to-main. A two-line tldraw patch keeps the stock **Edit link** item.

Shipped a bootstrap bug and caught it in verification: the patch first gated on
`meta.url` existing, so the menu item only appeared for shapes that already had a
link and the first one could never be added. Green on types, lint, build and CI.

Ran the full /create-pr pass. Phase 1 trimmed two over-long comments; the adherence
check caught inline styles `apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md` forbids; the delegated review
found a **real security bypass** — `new URL` strips leading control characters, so
`" obsidian://open?vault=Other&file=x"` passed the allowlist while a raw prefix test
said it wasn't an obsidian URL, meaning `preventDefault()` never ran and the URI
reached the OS handler. Reproduced, fixed, re-checked. Page links no longer go in
`href` at all. Four more review findings fixed, four listed as not-acted-on.

PR body rewritten with a Mermaid flow, a 5-row scenario matrix, screenshots
re-captured at the final revision, and a Not verified section. 5/5 CDP scenarios pass.

Since last time: branch merged with main (was 52 behind), unit tests removed at
Trang's request, and a standing rule added — never reply to a human reviewer without
drafting first.

content.text:
Yes — it changes the implementation substantially. Michael's #1442 review targets three things 2227 also does, and Roam has stronger reasons than Obsidian to switch.

## Michael's feedback, applied to 2227

| His point on #1442 | Where 2227 stands now |
|---|---|
| "Changes the built-in text shape's schema, adds a migration, and introduces custom link components" | All three: `TextShapeWithLinkUtil`, migration v6, and a copied `HyperlinkButton`. 2227 also changes the sync worker. |
| "Explore storing the link in `meta.url`… avoid backfilling existing text shapes" | We backfill every text shape in every canvas. |
| "A small pnpm patch if it lets us reuse those components instead of maintaining separate copies" | We keep a copy of `HyperlinkButton` and its icon. |
| "Compare the click behavior to… Discourse nodes" | The link icon opens a new tab. A Roam page link would reload the whole graph in that tab. |
| Loom surfaces: toolbar text, initial link, convert to node | Convert To reads only `props.text` ([uiOverrides.tsx:243](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx:243)), so the link is silently lost. |
| "Suspicious… how is this related?" | The worker hardening and `syncWorkerRoomSchema.test.ts`, which mirrors worker code without importing it, invite that same question. |

## My 14 Sep reasoning was wrong

I rejected `meta` because downgrading already breaks any canvas migrated to v5, so v6 seemed to cost nothing new. That doesn't hold. Each version bump locks out every collaborator who hasn't updated yet. v5 having done this once doesn't make v6 free.

This matters more in Roam than in Obsidian. A Roam graph has several people editing at once, and Roam Depot updates reach them at different times. When one person's build saves a v6 canvas, a teammate on the previous release gets `Incompatible schema?` and the canvas won't open.

With `meta` neither failure happens. On 14 Sep I tested stock tldraw 2.4.6 against a text shape carrying `meta.url`: it validates, and it round-trips. There's also no version bump. I haven't run an actual older extension build.

## Where Roam differs from Obsidian

- **The sync worker change goes away completely.** This is the biggest gain. The review's release-blocking bug was in that change, and so was the rule that the worker must deploy before the extension. Stock room schemas already accept `meta`, so the worker needs no change at all.
- **Patching is cheaper here.** Roam already patches tldraw 2.4.6, and the patch already re-exports internal components (`ToggleToolLockedButton`, `OverflowingToolbar`, `MobileStylePanel`). So we can export `EditLinkDialog` and `HyperlinkButton` and use them directly. Obsidian had to fork the dialog. Neither component, nor `useHasLinkShapeSelected`, is exported in 2.4.6 today.
- **Page links need no new format.** A Roam page URL is plain `https://`, which `T.linkUrl` already accepts. Obsidian had to work around `obsidian://`. What Roam needs is a click handler: clicking a link to a page in the same graph should navigate inside Roam instead of opening a new tab.
- **Validating the URL becomes our job, and it matters more here.** `props.url` was checked by `T.linkUrl` on every write. `meta` isn't checked at all. In a shared graph, another member or any API writer could store `javascript:` in `meta.url`, and it would reach an `href`. So we check it when saving in the dialog and again before rendering.

## Revised plan

**Remove:** `TextShapeWithLinkUtil`, `baseShapeUtils` and its four call sites, migration v6, all worker changes, the copied icon, `syncWorkerRoomSchema.test.ts` and `textShapeLinkStore.test.ts`. Most of #1441 goes.

**Add:**
1. **Patch additions.** Make `useHasLinkShapeSelected` accept any text shape (`|| type === "text"`). It must not depend on `meta.url` existing: 2228 did that, and a shape could never get its first link. Have `EditLinkDialog` read and write `meta.url` for text shapes. Export `HyperlinkButton`.
2. **Icon overlay.** Rendered from `InFrontOfTheCanvas` next to `DragHandleOverlay`, using the stock `HyperlinkButton`, placed just outside the right edge of the text (the position you liked).
3. **One click listener for geo and text icons.** If the link points to a page in the current graph, intercept the click: plain click opens it in the main window, shift-click opens it in the sidebar. Other URLs open in a new tab as they do now. Every check is based on the result of `new URL`, never a string-prefix test; 2228's bypass came from mixing the two.
4. **Pure helpers in `src/utils/`** for validation, `meta` read/write and page-link parsing. These are easy to unit test, so the `window` stubbing I fought with last time isn't needed.

**Carried over from 2228:** check the rendered screenshot (both tickets shipped the icon on top of the text), hand-edit the patch rather than running `pnpm patch-commit`, and draft any reply to Michael before posting.

**Spin off:** the worker's `{}` blanking is a real trap for future changes, but it doesn't belong in this PR. Creating that ticket needs the Linear connector, which isn't authorised in this session.

questions.question: How should text shapes reuse tldraw's Edit link dialog?

options.label: Patch the stock dialog (Recommended)
options.description: Add about 8 lines to the existing tldraw 2.4.6 patch so EditLinkDialog reads and writes meta.url for text. Nothing is copied, which matches Michael's preference. The catch: if Michael answers 2228's open question the other way, the two apps will differ.

options.label: Fork it like 2228
options.description: Copy the dialog the way 2228 did, so both apps work the same way. That means about 120 lines of copied code to maintain, which Michael said he'd rather avoid.

options.label: Wait for Michael on 2228
options.description: Hold this part until Michael answers 2228's patch-vs-hand-built question, then do the same here.

questions.question: What should clicking a text link to a page in the same graph do?

options.label: Click: main, shift: sidebar (Recommended)
options.description: Same as clicking a Roam page reference. Shift-click matches Discourse nodes (shift opens the sidebar). The icon needs no modifier for a plain click because clicking it doesn't select the shape. Applies to geo links too. External URLs still open a new tab.

options.label: Ctrl: main, shift: sidebar
options.description: Exactly the Discourse node modifiers. A plain click opens a new tab, as it does today.

options.label: Keep new-tab only
options.description: Every link opens a new tab, as it does now. Least work, but it's the inconsistency Michael called poor UX.

options.label: Keep, slimmed (Recommended)
options.description: Unit tests for the pure helpers only: URL validation, meta read/write, page-link parsing. This meets 2227's Done When, and these tests need no window stubs.

options.label: Drop, like 2228
options.description: Remove them for consistency with 2228. The fourth Done When item stays unmet; I'd say so in the PR body.

options.label: Drop it, state it (Recommended)
options.description: Keep the current behaviour and say in the PR that the link is dropped. A Discourse node already opens its own page on click, so a second link would compete with that. Show it in the Loom.

options.label: Carry it over
options.description: Copy meta.url onto the new node. It's kept, but the node gets two click targets, and Discourse nodes don't currently show a link icon.

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Agent-created Engineering tickets

For all agent-created Engineering tickets, including direct Linear tool calls and tickets created through other skills, use [dg-create-engineering-ticket](.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md). Create them in `Ticket Draft` with exactly one workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group: `Created by Claude`, `Created by Codex`, or `Created by LLM` for another or unknown agent. Record the creation skills actually used in `Notes`, and verify those fields after creation. If no skill was used, record `Created with: direct agent workflow (no skill)` and still apply the same review rules.

The requesting human reviews intent, scope, acceptance criteria, and ticket-writing standards before approving a move to `Triage` or `Backlog`. Keep the provenance label after approval. See the skill for transitions and missing-configuration handling. This applies to new tickets; do not retrospectively classify existing tickets.

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.
- Follow [PR_GUIDELINES.md](PR_GUIDELINES.md) for scope, verification, and review requirements. General code standards live in the style guide; app-specific instructions remain in nested `AGENTS.md` files.
- Before handoff or requesting review, run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` from `.agents/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check/SKILL.md` against the final diff and available PR metadata. Resolve findings or report them explicitly, including missing evidence. Rerun affected checks after changes.

ENG-2227 Store text shape links in meta and reuse tldraw's link UI

Text shapes keep their link in shape.meta.url, so the stock text schema is
unchanged: no migration, no sync worker change, and a canvas saved by this
build still opens in an older one, which ignores the link and round-trips it.

The existing tldraw patch now makes text shapes eligible for the stock Edit
link action unconditionally (gating on meta.url would stop a shape ever
getting its first link), has EditLinkDialog read and write meta.url for text,
and exports HyperlinkButton. An InFrontOfTheCanvas overlay renders that button
just outside each linked text shape, since text bounds hug their glyphs.

meta has no schema, so the overlay validates with T.linkUrl and renders the
parsed URL; relative paths linkUrl would resolve against a dummy origin are
rejected.

=================== PR_GUIDELINES.md
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.

**2. `getTextShapeLinkUrl` is in the wrong place.** It has one caller, the overlay, so the style guide says it should sit next to it rather than in `/utils`. I put it there because vitest only collects tests from `src/utils/__tests__`. But that limits where tests live, not where the code lives: existing tests in that folder already import from `~/components/canvas` (`autoCanvasRelationsSuppression`, `CustomStylePanel`). The fix is to move the helper next to the overlay and leave the test where it is.

**3. Done When #4 is only half met.** Link persistence has unit tests. Eligibility doesn't: it now lives in the tldraw patch, so it's only covered by the live run. Either say so in the Scope check or find a way to test it.

**4. Some inline styles could be Tailwind.** The overlay's fixed positioning (`absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none`) could be classes. The position values and the 44px size have to stay inline, because Roam's Tailwind is pre-JIT with 1rem = 14px. The root style copies `DragHandleOverlay`, so this one is a judgment call.

**5. Still outstanding:**
- **`$scope-check`:** blocked, because the Linear connector isn't authorised in this session. My draft assessment used Done When as fetched on 10 Sep, which may be stale.

**Not verified:** a sync-mode canvas, opening a canvas in an older extension build (argued and unit-tested against stock tldraw, not run), hiding below 32% zoom, locked shapes, and rotated or frame-clipped text. Separately, the loader reports one page error on every run, including runs with no canvas at all. It comes from the test account not being a graph admin.

Minor: the patch declares `HyperlinkButton` in the type definitions but only exports it from the ESM build. That matches how the existing patch handles its exports, and the Roam bundle uses ESM.
